checks.name: new bounds force the reported class

analyticCertificate: For nonnegative series, bounded increasing partial sums imply convergence. An upper bound by a convergent benchmark bounds every partial sum; a lower bound by a divergent benchmark forces unbounded partial sums. For an upper bound with p<=1, zero and the benchmark give opposite behaviors. For a lower bound with p>1, the benchmark and the constant sequence one give opposite behaviors; n^-p<=1 for every n>=1. These witnesses establish insufficiency, not merely failure of one proof method.
verification.scope: New finite-domain exact derivations plus displayed analytic hypotheses; frozen eight-instance review is not treated as extending admission.
